mainTopic: When רבי יהודה and the רבנן make a protective גזירה: חדש versus חמץ, the oil-filled eggshell, tying on שבת, and the sick בכור
overview: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה worries that a person handling חמץ might eat it, yet allows harvesting חדש before the עומר without that worry. רבא answers that חדש is harvested in an unusual way, which keeps the person alert. That answer is defeated by a משנה that allows normal harvesting of irrigated and valley fields. אביי then gives the lasting answer: people already keep away from חדש, but they eat חמץ all year. רבא shows that the רבנן are consistent too, since someone searching for חמץ in order to burn it will not eat it. רב אשי's alternative answer is rejected as a mistake. The גמרא then tests אביי's principle against cases of oil by a lamp and tying a bucket rope on שבת. It learns that the רבנן decree only where things are easily confused, and that for רבי יהודה a bow is itself a knot. Finally it challenges רבי יהודה from a sick בכור, and its answer, that a panicked owner may be careless, begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא on harvesting before the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא is quoted: רבי מאיר says people who harvest before the עומר act against the will of the חכמים, while רבי יהודה says they act with the חכמים' approval.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...they act against the will of the Sages.' These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: they were acting with the approval of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of a ברייתא about people who harvest new grain before the עומר is brought. This quote sets up the next move, a contradiction to רבי יהודה's ruling about חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the עומר is brought, new grain (חדש) may not be eaten. רבי מאיר disapproves of harvesting it then, apparently out of concern that the harvester might eat some. רבי יהודה approves of the harvesting, so he does not seem to share that concern.

keyTerms.meaning: With the approval of the Sages
Against the will of the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a quote that started on the previous page. The topic here is harvesting new grain before the עומר. It is not about חמץ yet. The link to חמץ comes in the next step.

phrases.english: they act against the will of the Sages,
phrases.notes: Refers to those who harvest before the עומר.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
they were acting with the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous page, which is being used to compare against רבי יהודה's view on חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר says harvesting before the עומר is against the חכמים' wishes, while רבי יהודה says it is with their approval.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יהודה worry here about eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה makes no גזירה about חדש, out of concern that the harvester will eat it, when he does make such a גזירה about חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why doesn't רבי יהודה make a decree here, out of concern that the person might come to eat from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. רבי יהודה worries about eating with חמץ, so why does he not worry about eating with חדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה said one should not handle (search for) חמץ once it is forbidden, in case one eats it. Handling forbidden חדש should raise the same worry. Yet he allows the harvesting, so his two rulings seem inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
Perhaps, out of concern that
He will come to eat from it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not decree
lest he come to eat from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא קָא גָזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא to challenge his consistency.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he fears eating when one handles חמץ, he should equally fear eating when one harvests חדש, yet he permits the harvesting.

steps.title: רבא: Unusual harvesting keeps him alert
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that חדש is different. Since it may only be harvested by hand-picking, the unusual method reminds the person that the grain is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: חדש is different. Since you only permitted him to harvest it by plucking by hand, he will remember.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction by pointing to a difference between חדש and חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the עומר, grain may be harvested only in an unusual way, by plucking. Doing the work in a strange manner keeps the person aware that the grain is forbidden, so he will not absent-mindedly eat it. Nothing like this exists with חמץ, so there the גזירה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
New grain, forbidden until the עומר is brought
Plucking by hand (an unusual way to harvest)
Remembers

phrases.english: Rava said:
New grain is different,
since you did not permit him
except by means of plucking,
he remembers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Handling חדש and handling חמץ carry the same risk of eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual hand-harvesting of חדש is a built-in reminder, so no גזירה is needed for it.

steps.title: אביי: What about grinding and sifting?
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the reminder works only during harvesting. Grinding and sifting seem to be done normally, so the worry should return at those stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: This works well at the time of plucking. But at the time of grinding and sifting, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer by pointing to later stages of processing the grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reminder comes from the unusual harvesting. After harvesting, the grain is ground and sifted, which seems to be done normally. At those stages there is no reminder, so the original worry should come back.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this part)
Grinding
Sifting
What can be said?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It works out well at the time of plucking,
but grinding and sifting,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reminder covers only the harvest. The later stages seem to be done normally, so the risk of eating returns there.

steps.title: Grinding and sifting are also unusual
steps.stepSummary: The answer given is that grinding and sifting are also done in an unusual way: grinding with a hand mill, and sifting on the back of the sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: grinding is done with a hand mill, and sifting is done on top of the sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by showing that every stage of processing חדש is done in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding is not done in a regular animal-powered or water-powered mill, only in a hand mill. Sifting is done on the back of the sieve, not in the usual way. So the reminder that comes from unusual work lasts through every stage, and רבא's answer still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
A hand mill
A sieve

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
grinding is with a hand mill,
sifting is on the back of a sieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's answer against אביי's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extending the same principle to later stages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grinding and sifting are done in the normal way.
steps.terutzMaskana: They too are done unusually, so the person stays alert throughout.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה on irrigated fields
steps.stepSummary: A משנה permits harvesting irrigated and valley fields before the עומר, and that משנה follows רבי יהודה. The word 'harvest' implies normal harvesting, so where is the reminder?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, regarding what we learned in a משנה: 'One may harvest irrigated fields and fields in the valleys, but one may not pile the grain', and we established that this משנה follows רבי יהודה. What is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: A stronger challenge is brought from a משנה, which suggests that רבי יהודה allows harvesting חדש even in the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'harvest' (קוצרין), which means regular reaping, not hand-plucking. Since this משנה follows רבי יהודה, he permits normal harvesting of חדש with no reminder at all. That undermines רבא's whole answer.

keyTerms.meaning: They harvest (in the normal way)
A field that needs irrigation
Piling the harvested grain into heaps
And we established (that it follows)

phrases.english: Rather, that which we learned:
One may harvest irrigated fields and those in the valleys,
phrases.notes: Their grain ripens early, before the עומר.

phrases.english: but one may not pile up the grain.
And we established it according to Rabbi Yehuda,
what is there to say!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 5 answered the first objection, this brings a stronger objection against רבא from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that חדש is harvested only by plucking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה following רבי יהודה permits regular harvesting, so there is no unusual method to serve as a reminder.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge succeeds. It forces the גמרא to give up רבא's approach and find a completely new reason.

steps.title: אביי: People already avoid new grain
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer. People already keep away from חדש, because it is forbidden all year until the עומר. They do not keep away from חמץ, because it is permitted all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: from חדש, a person keeps himself away. From חמץ, a person does not keep himself away.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי replaces רבא's answer with a new distinction between חדש and חמץ, which resolves the original contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each year's new grain stays forbidden for a long stretch until the עומר, so people are used to avoiding it and will not slip. חמץ is eaten freely all year and is forbidden only on פסח, so a person could easily eat it by habit. That is why רבי יהודה makes a גזירה only for חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: He keeps himself away from it
Leavened grain, forbidden on פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה worries about eating חמץ but not חדש. The reason is not how חדש is harvested, since רבא's answer was rejected. The reason is habit: people are used to staying away from חדש, but they eat חמץ all year.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אלא' ('rather') shows that רבא's answer is being dropped completely. Do not combine the two answers. אביי's reason stands by itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general principle about rabbinic decrees: a גזירה is needed where everyday habit makes a mistake likely, not where people are already trained to keep away.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
New grain: one keeps away from it,
leaven: one does not keep away from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 6, drops רבא's answer, and answers the original קשיא of step 2 in a new way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between חדש and חמץ depends on the unusual way חדש is harvested and processed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference depends on habit: people already keep away from חדש but not from חמץ.

steps.title: רבא asks why only רבי יהודה is questioned
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the רבנן also seem to contradict themselves, so the question should not be aimed only at רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it only רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה that is difficult? Is the רבנן against the רבנן not difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a sharp question: we pointed out a contradiction in רבי יהודה, but the רבנן seem to have the same kind of contradiction in reverse. This line sets up רבא's next move, where he answers both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are not worried that a person checking for חמץ will eat it, since they allow checking even later. But with חדש they are worried that a person will eat it. So the רבנן also look inconsistent, just in the opposite direction from רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or contradiction
One statement of רבי יהודה against another statement of רבי יהודה (an internal contradiction)
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not really asking a new question that he cannot answer. He raises the reverse contradiction so he can show that both sides can be explained.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda difficult,
while the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the discussion. After answering the contradiction in רבי יהודה, the גמרא notes that the רבנן face a parallel contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the רבנן's position on חמץ versus חדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן do not worry about eating during the search for חמץ, but they do worry about eating חדש. That is the same inconsistency charged against רבי יהודה, only reversed.

steps.title: Both contradictions are resolved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is already resolved by the earlier answer. The רבנן are resolved because a person searching for חמץ in order to burn it will not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not difficult, as we already answered. The רבנן against the רבנן is also not difficult: he himself is searching for it in order to burn it. Will he then eat from it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. רבי יהודה was already explained, and now he explains the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חמץ, the whole goal of searching is to destroy it, so the person's mind is focused on getting rid of it, not on eating it. With חדש, the person is preparing the grain as food, so there is a real worry he might eat it. That is why the רבנן worry about חדש but not about חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: As we already answered
Searches for it, seeks it out
In order to burn it
Will he eat from it? (rhetorical: of course not)

steps.whatToRemember: A person who is searching for חמץ in order to destroy it is not at risk of eating it. A person preparing חדש as food is at risk.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult —
as we answered.
The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult —
he himself is searching for it in order to burn it,
will he eat from it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the double question raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the person's mindset (destroying versus preparing food)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed inconsistent, worrying about eating חדש but not חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone searching to burn חמץ is focused on destroying it and will not eat it. Someone processing חדש is preparing food, so there is a real worry.

steps.title: רב אשי's alternative answer: only flour and roasted grain
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different answer for רבי יהודה: before the עומר, the grain was only processed into flour and roasted grain, so there was no worry about eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not difficult, because we learned in the משנה: 'flour and roasted grain.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own, different answer for the contradiction in רבי יהודה. He points to a משנה that says the markets were full of flour and roasted grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, before the עומר the חדש grain was only prepared as flour (קמח) or roasted grain (קלי). These were not foods people would simply grab and eat, so there was no worry. That would be a new way to explain why רבי יהודה is not worried here, different from the earlier answers of רבא and אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour
Roasted (parched) grain kernels

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
we learned 'flour and roasted grain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction in רבי יהודה, instead of the earlier answers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: only non-ready-to-eat forms of the grain were prepared
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חדש grain was handled in ways that might lead to eating it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only flour and roasted grain were made before the עומר, and these would not lead to accidental eating.

steps.title: רב אשי's answer is rejected as a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calls רב אשי's answer a mistake. It works from the roasted-grain stage onward, but not for the stages before the grain became roasted grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב אשי is a mistake. It works well from the roasted-grain stage onward, but from the beginning until it became roasted grain, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's answer. It points out a gap: before the grain became roasted grain, it went through stages where someone could have eaten it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי only explains why there is no worry once the grain is already flour or roasted grain. Before that, during harvesting and handling, the grain was in an edible state. So the worry about eating it is still there, and רב אשי's answer does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, an invented or unfounded statement
This works well for
From the beginning
What can be said? (there is no good answer)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's answer is rejected, because it does not cover the early stages before the grain became קלי. אביי's answer (people keep away from חדש but not from חמץ) stands.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that flour and roasted grain are a worry. It agrees there is no worry at that stage. The problem is only with the earlier stages before the grain reached that point.

phrases.english: This statement of Rav Ashi is a mistake:
that works well from roasted grain onward,
but from the beginning until roasted grain,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternative answer offered in step 10.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answer only covers the grain after it became flour or roasted grain. It ignores the earlier stages, when the grain could have been eaten.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's answer fails, so the contradiction in רבי יהודה must be resolved the way אביי did: people keep away from חדש but not from חמץ.

steps.title: Blocking a defense of רב אשי based on רבא's unusual harvesting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines someone defending רב אשי by saying the unusual way of harvesting (קיטוף) reminds people not to eat the grain. It rejects this, because a source following רבי יהודה allows certain fields to be harvested in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that the unusual way of harvesting (קיטוף), like רבא said, reminds people not to eat it: but there is the source 'One may harvest irrigated fields and fields in the valleys' in the normal way, and we said it follows רבי יהודה. What can you say about that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to rescue רב אשי by borrowing רבא's idea that the grain was harvested in an unusual way. It then knocks that rescue down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gap in רב אשי's answer was the time before the grain became roasted grain. What would remind people not to eat it then? רבא's idea fills that gap: the unusual harvesting is the reminder. But a source that follows רבי יהודה allows irrigated fields and valley fields to be harvested in the normal way before the עומר, so there is no unusual sign, and the gap comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a possible defense in order to reject it)
Plucking or cutting in an unusual way, done so people notice it is different
An irrigated field, which needs to be watered by hand
And we established (that this source follows a certain opinion)
What can be said? (there is no good answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on רבא himself. The גמרא is only showing that רבא's idea cannot save רב אשי's answer, because the source shows normal harvesting was allowed according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא עַל יְדֵי קִיטּוּף כִּדְרָבָא,
phrases.english: And if you say: through unusual harvesting, like Rava said,
phrases.notes: A possible defense: the odd way of harvesting itself reminds people not to eat the grain.

phrases.english: but [what about] 'One may harvest irrigated fields and those in the valleys',
phrases.notes: These fields may be harvested before the עומר in the normal way.

phrases.english: and we established it according to Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: So רבי יהודה himself allows normal harvesting here, with no unusual sign.

phrases.english: what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The defense fails.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא עַל יְדֵי קִיטּוּף כִּדְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rejection of רב אשי from Step 11 by closing off a possible rescue.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבא's קיטוף idea to fill the gap in רב אשי's answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי יהודה, some fields are harvested normally before the עומר, so there is no unusual sign to remind people.

steps.title: Final verdict that רב אשי's answer is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Since the defense failed, the גמרא concludes again that רב אשי's answer is a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the answer of רב אשי is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this side discussion with its final verdict: רב אשי's answer does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא said this before Step 12 and now repeats it on purpose. Even after trying to defend it, רב אשי's answer still cannot explain the time before the roasted-grain stage. This leaves אביי's answer from Step 7 as the working explanation for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An invented or mistaken statement
Rather (here it introduces the conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's answer is rejected. What remains is אביי's principle: people naturally keep away from חדש but not from חמץ.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi's [answer] is a mistake.
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats its earlier verdict, now final after the failed defense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the failed defense in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's answer is rejected, and אביי's answer remains.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really make a גזירה whenever people don't naturally keep away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions אביי's principle. Does רבי יהודה really make a protective decree every time people do not naturally keep away from something?
steps.simpleTranslation: And anywhere that a person does not keep away from something, does רבי יהודה make a protective decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges אביי's principle. This line sets up the challenge, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From Step 7, it sounds as if רבי יהודה makes a גזירה whenever people do not naturally stay away from a forbidden thing. The גמרא asks whether that is really his general rule. The question is worded as a question, but it works as an attack, and the next step brings evidence against the idea.

keyTerms.meaning: He keeps away from it
Made a protective rabbinic decree (גזירה)
Does...? (a question that expects the answer 'no')

phrases.english: And anywhere that one does not keep away from it,
phrases.notes: Refers to things people are not used to avoiding, like חמץ during the year.

phrases.english: does Rabbi Yehuda make a decree?
phrases.notes: Hints that רבי יהודה does not always do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּלָא בָּדֵיל מִינֵּיהּ מִי גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting רב אשי aside, the גמרא returns to test אביי's principle from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's principle that רבי יהודה makes a גזירה wherever people do not naturally keep away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were his rule, he should make a גזירה in every such case. A source will show he does not.

steps.title: The eggshell of oil by the lamp: רבי יהודה is lenient
steps.stepSummary: A משנה forbids putting an oil-filled eggshell next to a lamp on שבת, because someone might take oil from it. רבי יהודה permits it, even though people do not usually keep away from oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: A person may not make a hole in an eggshell, fill it with oil, and put it next to the lamp so that it drips oil into the lamp, and this applies even if it is made of earthenware. And רבי יהודה permits it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as proof for its challenge. Here רבי יהודה does not make a גזירה, even though oil is something people do not usually avoid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worry that someone will take oil out of the shell, which lowers the oil feeding the lamp. That counts as putting out the flame, which is forbidden on שבת. Oil is not something people naturally avoid. So if אביי's rule were true, רבי יהודה should agree to the decree here. Instead he permits it, which seems to contradict אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A tube or hollow shell
Drips
Earthenware or clay
Permits

steps.confusionAlert: Earthenware is mentioned to show how strict the חכמים are. Even oil sitting in a clay tube, which people find unpleasant to use, is still forbidden by the חכמים.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: A person may not pierce
phrases.notes: Introduces the משנה (שבת 29b).

phrases.english: an eggshell and fill it with oil
and place it beside the lamp
so that it will drip,
phrases.notes: The extra oil drips in and makes the lamp burn longer.

phrases.english: and even if it is of earthenware.
phrases.notes: The חכמים still forbid it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda permits!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה makes no גזירה here, even though people do not avoid oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן לֹא יִקּוֹב אָדָם שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that רבי יהודה does not always make a גזירה when people do not naturally keep away.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about an oil-filled eggshell placed beside a lamp.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle drawn from אביי that רבי יהודה makes a גזירה wherever people do not naturally keep away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People do not avoid oil, yet רבי יהודה permits the oil-filled eggshell beside the lamp and makes no גזירה.

steps.title: On שבת people are extra careful and keep away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that on שבת people treat the rules seriously and naturally keep away from the lamp. So this case also counts as something people keep away from.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, because of the seriousness of שבת, people do keep away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי's principle by explaining why the lamp case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil is normally not something people avoid. But on שבת, people are so careful about putting out a flame that they stay away from the lamp and anything next to it. So the lamp case fits the 'people keep away' group, and אביי's rule that רבי יהודה makes no גזירה in such cases still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other case)
The seriousness of שבת
They definitely keep away

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's principle survives: רבי יהודה makes no גזירה where people naturally keep away. This includes things on שבת, because people are extra careful then.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether people 'keep away' can depend on the setting. The same oil is avoided on שבת because of how seriously people take the day.

phrases.english: There, because of the stringency of Shabbat,
they certainly keep away.
phrases.notes: So no גזירה is needed, and רבי יהודה can permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם חוּמְרָא דְּשַׁבָּת מִבְדָּל בְּדִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 14 and 15 by showing the lamp case is one where people keep away.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil is something people do not avoid, so רבי יהודה's leniency would contradict אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת people do keep away from the lamp, so the case fits אביי's principle.

steps.title: A second שבת case: the snapped bucket rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a bucket rope that snapped on שבת, to compare it with the oil-eggshell case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raised a contradiction between one שבת law and another שבת law. A ברייתא teaches that if a bucket rope snaps, a person may not tie it with a knot, but he may tie it with a bow. רבי יהודה says he may wrap a money belt or a sash around it, as long as he does not tie it with a bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings a new source about a snapped rope, which it will soon compare against the oil-eggshell משנה from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying a real knot (קשירה) on שבת is forbidden. The תנא קמא allows a bow (עניבה) to fix the rope. רבי יהודה forbids even a bow and only allows wrapping a belt around the rope. So in this case רבי יהודה is the strict one.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)
Tying a real knot, which is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת
Tying a bow (a loose, easily untied loop)
A money belt (a hollow belt)
A sash or wide belt

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. In the oil case, רבי יהודה was lenient. Here, רבי יהודה is the strict one and the תנא קמא is lenient. That reversal is the whole basis for the next step.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction between a Shabbat law and a Shabbat law,
phrases.notes: The oil-eggshell law versus the rope law.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
A bucket rope that snapped,
he should not tie it with a knot, but rather tie it with a bow.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
he wraps a money belt or a sash around it,
as long as he does not tie it with a bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second שבת source to set against the oil-eggshell משנה from Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The opinions of רבי יהודה and the רבנן regarding protective decrees on שבת

steps.title: Both sides seem to contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself, and so do the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty between one statement of רבי יהודה and another statement of רבי יהודה. There is also a difficulty between one statement of the רבנן and another statement of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the double contradiction openly. Each side is lenient in one case and strict in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the oil, the רבנן forbid out of fear that a person will take oil, while רבי יהודה permits. With the rope, the רבנן permit a bow and do not worry it will lead to a knot, while רבי יהודה forbids a bow. Each side seems to make a protective decree in one case and refuse it in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (a contradiction or challenge)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: There is a difficulty between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: He is lenient on the oil but strict on the bow.

phrases.english: and a difficulty between the Rabbis and the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: They are strict on the oil but lenient on the bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the contradiction that comes from comparing Step 17 with Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יהודה and the רבנן about protective decrees on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side makes a protective decree in one case and refuses one in a parallel case, which looks inconsistent.

steps.title: The Rabbis: oil gets confused with oil, but a bow does not get confused with a knot
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן are consistent. A decree is needed only where people are likely to confuse the permitted act with the forbidden one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction in the רבנן is not difficult. One use of oil can easily be confused with another use of oil. But tying a bow is not confused with tying a knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in the רבנן. It shows a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil in the eggshell and oil in the lamp are the same substance. A person used to taking oil for other purposes could easily take this oil too, so the רבנן make a decree. A bow and a knot are clearly different actions, so there is no real risk of mixing them up, and no decree is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It gets confused or mixed up with
It is not difficult (the opening of an answer)

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult:
oil with oil gets confused,
a bow with a knot does not get confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the double contradiction from Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן decree in one case and not in the other for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן decree only where confusion is likely. Oil is confused with oil, but a bow is not confused with a knot.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a bow simply is a knot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is not making a decree in the rope case. He holds that a bow itself counts as a forbidden knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction in רבי יהודה is not difficult. רבי יהודה does not forbid a bow as a decree to keep people away from a knot. Rather, he holds that a bow itself is a knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבי יהודה. It explains that his strictness about the bow is not a protective decree at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that רבי יהודה forbids a bow only as a fence around tying a knot. The גמרא says no: for him, a bow is actually a real קשירה. So in the rope case he makes no decree, and his refusal to decree in the oil case stays consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: He decreed (made a protective rabbinic rule)
Because of, out of concern for
He holds, he is of the opinion
Itself

steps.whatToRemember: The double contradiction is resolved. The רבנן decree only where confusion is realistic (oil with oil), not where it is not (a bow with a knot). רבי יהודה's ban on a bow is not a decree, because for him a bow is a full knot.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה is being 'stricter with decrees' in the rope case. His strictness there comes from how he defines a knot, not from a decree.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
the reason of Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּגָזַר עֲנִיבָה אַטּוּ קְשִׁירָה,
phrases.english: is not because he decrees against a bow out of concern for a knot,
but rather because he holds
that a bow itself is a knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the double contradiction from Step 18, completing the resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason behind the ruling (it is a direct prohibition, not a decree)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids a bow as a protective decree against tying a knot, which would clash with his refusal to decree in the oil case.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, a bow is itself a forbidden knot, so no decree is involved and he stays consistent.

steps.title: A second contradiction within the Rabbis' rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in which the רבנן forbid tying a bucket with a rope and רבי יהודה permits it. This sets up a contradiction with the רבנן's view in the previous ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis' view was contrasted with another view of the Rabbis, as we learned in a משנה: One may tie a bucket with a sash, but not with a rope, and רבי יהודה permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new contradiction, this time between two rulings of the רבנן. Here it only quotes the source. The actual problem is spelled out in step 24, after the גמרא first clarifies in steps 22–23 what kind of rope the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous ברייתא the רבנן were lenient about a bow (עניבה) and did not decree against it because of a knot. Now a משנה shows them being strict about tying a bucket with a rope. Before the גמרא can show the clash, it must figure out what rope is being discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a contradiction (set two sources against each other)
A bucket (used to draw water from a well)
A sash or belt (a cloth band, not a rope)
A rope

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
One may tie a bucket with a sash
phrases.notes: A sash is not normally left tied, so tying it does not make a lasting knot.

phrases.english: but not with a rope,
and Rabbi Yehuda permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the first set of contradictions in steps 18–20, the גמרא raises a fresh contradiction within the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the רבנן, who in step 19 refused to decree on a bow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן forbid tying a bucket with a rope, they appear to be making a decree. That clashes with their refusal to decree in the bow case.

steps.title: What kind of rope does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which rope the משנה is talking about. It rules out an ordinary rope, because tying an ordinary rope to a bucket makes a permanent knot, which רבי יהודה could never permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rope of what kind? If you say an ordinary rope, would רבי יהודה permit that? It is a permanent knot, because he will certainly leave it there and stop using the rope for anything else!
steps.whatsHappening: Before the contradiction can be stated, the גמרא pauses to clarify the case. It asks what type of rope is meant and rejects the first possibility, an ordinary rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary rope tied to a bucket stays there for good, so the knot is a קשר של קיימא. Tying such a knot is a real Torah-level מלאכה. רבי יהודה's leniency proves the משנה cannot mean that kind of rope.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary, everyday rope
A permanent knot (forbidden on שבת by Torah law)
To set aside / dedicate it permanently (leaving the rope there for good)

phrases.english: A rope of what kind?
If you say an ordinary rope,
would "Rabbi Yehuda permit" it?
It is a permanent knot,
since he will certainly leave it there for good!
phrases.notes: Once tied to the bucket, the rope stays there permanently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It clarifies the case in the משנה just quoted, so the contradiction can be stated precisely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of rope the משנה refers to.

steps.title: The משנה means a weaver's rope
steps.stepSummary: The rope in the משנה must be a weaver's rope. A weaver needs his rope for work, so he will not leave it tied to the bucket permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the משנה means a weaver's rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the משנה is talking about a weaver's rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A weaver will untie his rope and take it back for his work, so the knot is only temporary and not a Torah violation. This explains why רבי יהודה permits it. It also means the רבנן's ban must be a rabbinic decree, which is exactly what sets up the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A weaver
It is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: Once the rope is a weaver's rope, tying it is NOT a Torah prohibition at all. Any ban by the רבנן is only a decree (גזירה), and that is the whole point of the coming question.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it means a weaver's rope.
phrases.notes: A weaver needs his rope back, so the knot is temporary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה speaks of a weaver's rope, whose knot is only temporary.

steps.title: Do the Rabbis decree here but not with the bow?
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is now stated directly. The רבנן decree against a weaver's rope because of an ordinary rope, yet they did not decree against a bow because of a knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did the רבנן really decree against a weaver's rope because of an ordinary rope?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the rope is identified, the גמרא states the contradiction: the רבנן made a decree here, so why not in the bow case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying a weaver's rope is permitted by Torah law, so forbidding it must be a decree, made to prevent people from tying ordinary ropes. In the bow case the רבנן refused a similar decree. On the surface they look inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: They decreed (made a protective rabbinic ban)
Because of / on account of (worry about another case)

phrases.english: And did the Rabbis decree against a weaver's rope
because of an ordinary rope?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַרוּ רַבָּנַן חֶבֶל דְּגַרְדִּי אַטּוּ חֶבֶל דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes the contradiction opened in step 21, now that step 23 has defined the case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's consistency about when to make decrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן decree against a harmless weaver's rope but not against a harmless bow, even though both seem to involve the same kind of risk.

steps.title: A rope can be mistaken for a rope, but a bow can't be mistaken for a knot
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the רבנן decree here, because one rope is easily confused with another. A bow, however, is never confused with a knot, so no decree is needed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A rope with a rope can be mixed up, but a bow with a knot cannot be mixed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן are consistent: they decree only where people could actually confuse the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ropes look alike, so someone allowed to tie a weaver's rope may end up tying an ordinary rope permanently. A bow and a knot are clearly different actions, so permitting one will not lead to the other. This applies the rule from step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be confused / mixed up
A bow (a loose loop that is easy to untie)
Tying a knot

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן decree only when the permitted thing looks like the forbidden thing. Rope vs. rope is easy to confuse, so they decree. Bow vs. knot is not confused, so they do not.

phrases.english: Yes, a rope with a rope can be confused,
but a bow with a knot is not confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the contradiction stated in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by how likely confusion is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed inconsistent, decreeing in one case and not in a similar one.
steps.terutzMaskana: A decree is made only where the permitted act can be confused with the forbidden one. Ropes can be confused; a bow and a knot cannot.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really never decree when people keep away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יהודה does not decree where people naturally stay away from the forbidden act. It brings a ברייתא about a בכור with a blood condition, where he forbids bloodletting even if the animal will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And wherever a person keeps away from the forbidden act, does רבי יהודה not decree? But it was taught in a ברייתא: A בכור that has a blood buildup, even if it will die, one may not let its blood. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יהודה and challenges his supposed rule of not decreeing where people stay away from the forbidden act. It brings a ברייתא where he seems to be strict anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהודה was understood to avoid decrees where people naturally keep their distance (step 16). A בכור is holy, and people are very careful not to harm it. Yet רבי יהודה forbids any bloodletting, even to save its life, which looks like a strict decree in exactly such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: He keeps away from it (naturally avoids the forbidden act)
A firstborn kosher animal, holy and given to a כהן
Its blood is congested (a buildup of blood that endangers it)
Letting blood (cutting to release blood)

steps.confusionAlert: Wounding a בכור can give it a blemish (מום), which is forbidden to cause on purpose. The question is not about שבת. It tests whether רבי יהודה's 'no decree where people keep away' rule holds up in a different area of הלכה.

phrases.english: And wherever one keeps away from it,
does Rabbi Yehuda not decree?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
A firstborn animal that has a blood buildup,
even if it will die,
one may not let its blood,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּבָדֵיל מִינֵּיהּ לָא גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the רבנן's consistency, the גמרא returns to test רבי יהודה's principle of not decreeing where people keep away.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that רבי יהודה does not decree where people naturally avoid the forbidden act.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a holy בכור people are naturally careful, yet רבי יהודה still forbids all bloodletting, even at the cost of the animal's life. That looks like a decree in a case where people keep away.

steps.title: The Sages' view in the ברייתא: bloodletting is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the opinion of the חכמים: one may let blood from the sick בכור, as long as he does not make a מום on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He may let its blood, as long as he does not make a blemish on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 26 by giving the other opinion, the חכמים. This completes the challenge against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allow the bloodletting and only warn against making a מום. רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting completely, even if the animal will die, because he is worried the person will end up making a מום. So רבי יהודה does make a גזירה here, even though people normally keep away from damaging a holy בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי יהודה
He may let blood (cut a vein to release blood)
As long as / on condition that
Make a blemish on it. A בכור with a מום can no longer be offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: These words do not answer the challenge. They are the end of the ברייתא that the challenge is built on. The answer starts with the word הָתָם.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: he may let blood,
phrases.notes: The other side of the ברייתא, arguing with רבי יהודה

phrases.english: provided that he does not inflict a blemish on it.
phrases.notes: He must take care to let blood in a spot where the cut does not count as a מום

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Step 26, which sets up the challenge against רבי יהודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, one may let blood from a sick בכור as long as he does not make a מום. רבי יהודה forbids it entirely.

steps.title: A בכור is different because the owner is panicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. In the case of the בכור, a person is panicked and anxious about losing his animal, so even רבי יהודה makes a גזירה there. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since a person is panicked and anxious...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge by saying the בכור case is special. This is only the opening of the answer, and it finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually people stay away from damaging a holy בכור, so no גזירה should be needed. But when the animal is about to die, the owner is worried about losing it. In that state he may not be careful and could make a מום, so רבי יהודה forbids bloodletting entirely. The usual reason people stay away does not work when a person is panicked.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that other case. Used to set a case apart from the one being discussed
Since / because
Panicked, rushed, anxious
A person panics over losing his money or property (the full idea behind this answer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יהודה can be consistent. He does not make a גזירה where people naturally stay away from the forbidden act, unless panic over a loss is likely to make them careless.

phrases.english: There, since a person is agitated
phrases.notes: The answer is cut off here and continues on the next amud: he panics about his property, so he may come to make a מום.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the בכור case showed that רבי יהודה makes a גזירה even where people naturally stay away from the forbidden act.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור is an exception. The owner is panicked about losing his animal, so his usual caution cannot be relied on, and a גזירה is needed.
